intent_snapshot.goal: unified-lane-sessions S7 (#570; Spec docs/specs/unified-lane-sessions.spec.md D12, D19, BR-DEC-1, BR-DEC-4, BR-SCN-6). Authority-path change. Add findActiveLaneBatchForTask(root, taskId) (failing closed on corrupt or ambiguous multi-batch matches) so findLaneRelayTarget and breaking-revision approval reach any child of a single-task or Initiative v3 batch through the record-level rebindBatchChildIdentity and hasContiguousLaneRebind proven in S3; trigger advanceLanes after relayLaneDecision so answered decisions reset no_progress and resume, native-gated stop closes only that child's session and retains its Lane, and coordinator: correct rotates to g(n+1).

acceptance.assertion: In tests/single-task-lane-decision.test.ts: findActiveLaneBatchForTask locates Child 2 in a two-child Initiative batch; relaying a literal-user decision resumes Child 2 via advanceLanes with no_progress reset to 0 while Child 1 is untouched; native-gated stop stops Child 2's session via BatchSessionPort.stop, parks Child 2 lane_executor_stopped, retains Child 2's Lane, and leaves Child 1 running; a coordinator: correct instruction closes g1 with proof and opens g2; an unknown task returns relayed false, and two active batches claiming the same task_id fail closed.

In tests/single-task-lane-decision.test.ts and tests/unattended-contracts.test.ts: approving a breaking intent revision for one child in a two-child Initiative calls rebindBatchChildIdentity, appends lane_rebinds, advances plan_digest, and continues without batch_plan_changed or retire_stale_batch (including after a Revision Delegation reseal), while refusing a stale from_digest.

lane_decision.ts never mentions plan_source; drive-batch.md and drive.md describe per-child decision relay, native-gated stop, and lane_rebinds; dist consistency, bundles, mirrors, and typecheck pass.

attestations.summary: Round-3 delta: validateLaneRecordShape now meets the last reseal at lane_rebinds[0].from_digest (identical in both runtime mirrors and both dist bundles; no runtime writer appends reseals after rebinds), and tests drive relay and post-rebind continuation (incl. after a Delegation reseal) through real startLanes/advanceLanes; blast radius medium — persisted batch_run_state/v3 validation in batch_state.ts.

advisory_findings.summary: validateLaneRebinds checks only the last rebind's to_digest against plan_digest; intermediate links (rebinds[i].to_digest === rebinds[i+1].from_digest) are not validated at load, so the reseal-to-rebind handoff check anchors on an unverified chain head.

evidence.trigger: a stored record with two lane_rebinds whose first to_digest differs from the second from_digest, and reseals ending at rebinds[0].from_digest → loads without a shape error

findings.summary: Native-gated per-child stop only reaches BatchSessionPort.stop when HostRuntime has an injected sessionPortFactory, which production Claude/Pi/Antigravity Hosts never supply; production stop falls back to stopSingleTaskSupervisor and leaves the child's Herdr session running.

evidence.trigger: Production Host (HostRuntime constructed without options.sessionPortFactory, as in host-core/mcp_runtime.ts:329 and .pi-extension/imm-unattended-batch.ts:157 which only forward it when a test passes one) relays a native-gated stop for Child 2 of an S5 port-based batch (session_provider 'herdr', child.session.handle set, no executor_mode) → runtime.ts:827 skips SessionPortAdapter construction, relayLaneDecision gets no `sessions`, falls through to stopSingleTaskSupervisor, so BatchSessionPort.stop is never called and Child 2's Herdr session keeps running (and is not parked lane_executor_stopped via the port path). lane_sessions/index.ts portFor already falls back to the registry descriptor factory when createPort is absent; the stop path lacks that fallback. The host-level tests pass only because claudeHarness/piHarness (and the Pi shared runtime monkey-patch in tests/single-task-lane-decision.test.ts) inject a factory. Fix: build the stop port from SESSION_PROVIDER_REGISTRY (same resolution as portFor) when no factory is injected, and add a test that pins stop on a HostRuntime without sessionPortFactory using a registered test provider.

findings.summary: The two-child Initiative resume test injects a fake `advance` that writes no_progress=0 itself, so advanceLanes is never exercised for Child 2 and 'Child 1 untouched' is asserted only against the fake.

evidence.trigger: Two-child Initiative batch (s7Fixture), relayLaneDecision for child-2 with a test-supplied advance that rewrites child-2 session {no_progress:0, baseline:'r2'} → the asserted reset and sibling invariance come from the test's own write; the production HostRuntime path (advance = startPreparedBatch(initiativeSlug, {reuseOnly}) → advanceLanes over every child) could leave no_progress unreset or mutate child-1's session and this test would still pass
